verses.text: After this David defeated the Philistines, brought them under his rule, and took control of their principal city.

David defeated Moab and made the captives lie on the ground. He measured them off with a line, putting two lengths to death and sparing one full length. The Moabites became his subjects and paid him tribute.
David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as Hadadezer went to restore his rule at the Euphrates.
David captured seventeen hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung the chariot horses but kept enough for a hundred chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.
David stationed troops in the territory of Damascus. The Syrians became his subjects and paid him tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
King David took a large amount of bronze from Betah and Berothai, two of Hadadezer's cities.
When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army,
he sent his son Joram to greet King David and congratulate him on defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi. Joram brought objects made of silver, gold, and bronze.
King David dedicated these to the LORD along with the silver and gold he had set apart from all the nations he'd subdued.
They came from Syria, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
David stationed troops all across Edom, and all the Edomites became his subjects. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David ruled over all Israel and did what was just and right for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was the scribe.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons served as chief ministers.
